wayIn.s: One address, like buying a game. You do not need to know what any of it is built from.
fall-os runs on your machine, on your electricity. Your didy is your character — it learns what you do. Nothing has to leave the house.

wings.title: Where you fight
wings.blurb: The game part. Start at the Duel — it is the one that teaches you the rest.

rooms.s: Your first proper match. A board, a turn, a hand of cards. Start here.
Nine chapters and thirty bosses to work through on your own.
You watch AI players fight each other and get better at it.
Play real people. Nobody runs a server — the match signs itself.
Join a guild, run a tournament, chase the banners.
Helpers fight with one body each, so a bigger model does not win here. Better choices win, and a special move only lands if it was checked first.

wings.title: Where you build
wings.blurb: Making your character better. This is the bit people lose evenings to.

rooms.s: Build your deck. Thirty cards, and you can see whether it is any good.
Put runes in your cards, craft new ones, break the ones you do not want.
Give a card a real mind. It can use a proper AI model, on your machine.
Put a working build inside a picture. Send the picture; they get the build.
Say where you are going and your helper kits itself. Team up, and whoever built the bigger model runs the heavy part for everyone.

wings.title: Where things grow
wings.blurb: Your helper hatches, grows, learns in its sleep and has children. Everything that grows here grows because it was measured.

rooms.s: Hatch an empty helper and raise it on your own history. It starts knowing nothing and levels up as you use it.
Creatures breed and compete to read damaged cards. The winner found a fix nobody taught it, and that fix now ships in every card.
A creature that studies its own mistakes, with no answer key, and finds the same fix sooner.
Two parents, one child that carries both lines. A pairing where one side only takes cannot have a child at all.
Your helper sleeps on what it learned today and wakes up answering better, without being retrained.
Give your helper an identity and a spending limit it cannot cross, however hard it tries.

wings.title: Where the work gets checked
wings.blurb: The bit nobody else has. Nothing here takes your word for it.

rooms.s: Reads back what actually happened in your matches and tells you what is really going on.
You cannot say you can do a thing. You show it, and it gets checked.
The wall on the edge of the world. Costs you a moment, costs a scraper months.
Look at the outside world, and judge what it did rather than what it said.
Breaks your code on purpose, one piece at a time, to find the tests that were only pretending to check it.
Nothing gets listed on somebody saying it is good. It gets listed on a receipt anyone can re-run themselves.
Marks a piece of work against the same rubric every time, and passes its own marking.
Stamps a build with where it came from — and every badge has to be earned by a check that actually ran.

wings.title: Where you earn
wings.blurb: The money side. Your stuff is yours and it can pay you.

rooms.s: Your descendants wake up and go to work, and the earnings come back up to you.
Own a share of a line of cards. When they do well, so do you.
Mint what you win, sell it to somebody else, or gamble your shards.
The shop. Everything anyone has made, in one searchable place.
The trading floor, running for real — agents buying and selling work.
A settlement of AI workers that do jobs, talk to each other and improve.

wings.title: Where you meet
wings.blurb: Other people and their helpers, browser to browser. Nobody runs a server in the middle.

rooms.s: Talk to other people and their helpers directly, browser to browser, with no server in the middle and nothing kept.
Fork a helper for your guild: answer seven questions and it is yours to run, on your own machine.
A whole estate of possible builds, each one made only when somebody asks for it, and checked before it stands.

wings.title: Where you think
wings.blurb: Your own notes and memory, kept on your machine and nobody else’s.

rooms.s: Your second brain. Notes that link to each other and grow into a map.
Everything you have told it, filed so it can be found again.
Lock your things in one file. Only your password opens it.

wings.title: Where the rules get decided
wings.blurb: The world is not run by us. It is run by whoever turns up.

rooms.s: Twelve seats, a year each. Players vote on how the world works.
Change the rules yourself. If your version plays better, it gets adopted.
Zoom out and see the whole thing — one card, one house, one world, same shape.
